properties.title: FeO Abundance · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Clementine UVVIS DIM Mosaic (5 bands: 415, 750, 900, 950, 1000 nm, 100 m/pixel) combined with OMAT as a 6-element input vector. 1D CNN: two Conv1D layers (32 filters, kernel=2, ReLU), MaxPooling1D (pool=2), Dense(64, ReLU), single linear output. L2 regularization (0.001) on all layers. Adam optimizer (lr=0.01), max 400 epochs, early stopping (patience=30), z-score normalization. Trained on 49 ground-truth points from Apollo, Luna, and Chang'E missions including Chang'E-6 (first farside samples). R²=0.96+ on training set; LOOCV R²=0.897.
properties.lri:data_use_note: High-resolution FeO abundance at 100 m/pixel — 600× finer than LP GRS (60 km). Primary indicator for iron-rich basaltic maria. Combined with TiO₂ identifies ilmenite-rich zones (FeTiO₃), the leading ISRU target for oxygen and metal extraction. CNN model outperforms classical equation approaches in high-FeO regions (>24 wt%), confirmed by LP GRS and Chang'E-5 sample measurements.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: 1D CNN inversion from Clementine UVVIS, calibrated with Chang'E-6 samples. LOOCV R²=0.897. Global mean 8.48 wt%; maria 17.71 wt%. Higher accuracy than classical equation model in high-FeO regions (>24 wt%), consistent with LP GRS observations.
properties.lri:quality_note: FeO abundance derived from 1D CNN inversion of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). The model uses 49 ground-truth samples including the first farside samples from Chang'E-6, providing a calibration point previously unavailable for the lunar far side. LOOCV R²=0.897, RMSE=1.37 wt% (leave-one-out cross-validation). Global mean 8.48 wt%, unimodal distribution with mode 5.28 wt% — consistent with LP GRS global measurement of 4.7 wt%. CNN FeO estimates are ~0.25 wt% higher globally than the companion equation model, and ~0.88 wt% higher in maria. The CNN model captures nonlinear reflectance-composition relationships missed by classical equations, yielding more accurate estimates in high-FeO maria such as Oceanus Procellarum (CNN: >24 wt%; Equation: ~21 wt%), consistent with LP GRS and Chang'E-5 sample measurements (FeO: 24.7 wt%). High-FeO material (>15 wt%) in the lunar south polar region (>65°S) is identified in basin floors, crater walls, and central peaks — the first FeO mapping with full polar coverage beyond 65°. Key limitation: ground truth remains sparse at high latitudes; calibration is extrapolated from mid-to-low latitude sample sites.
